Q: Iterate a list inside a list (cartesian product of two lists) A:

You can flatMap the list of uuids:

List<Boolean> collect = 
    Stream.of(DaysOfWeekEnum.values())
          .flatmap(day -> uuidList.stream()
                                  .map(uuid -> resolver.calculateForDay(day, uuid))
          .collect(Collectors.toList());

Q: ggplot2 color gradient per group A:

This is an old question but I recently got frustrated enough with it that I built my own ggplot2 extension to handle it. With ggtintshade, you can separately specify the color and the shade of the points, making this trivial.

install.packages("ggtintshade")
library(ggtintshade)
library(plyr)

find_hull <- function(df) df[chull(df$Sepal.Length, df$Sepal.Width), ]
hulls <- ddply(iris, "Species", find_hull)

ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width, shape=Species, 
                 color=Species, size=Petal.Width)) + 
  geom_point_tintshade(aes(tintshade = Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_polygon(data = hulls, alpha = 0.15, size=0.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(15,16,17)) +
  scale_size(guide = "none") +
  ggtitle("Sepal.Length vs. Sepal.Width - size Petal.Width") +
  scale_tintshade_continuous(guide = guide_tintshade(type="crossed"))

Not only does this make the colors both lighter and darker, it also adds a clean legend to the plot mapping this new aesthetic.

To answer @Ivo's comment as well, this package plays nicely with other ggplot2 functions so you can literally just tell it which colors you'd like it to be:

ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width, shape=Species, 
                 color=Species, size=Petal.Width)) + 
  geom_point_tintshade(aes(tintshade = Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_polygon(data = hulls, alpha = 0.15, size=0.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(15,16,17)) +
  scale_size(guide = "none") +
  ggtitle("Sepal.Length vs. Sepal.Width - size Petal.Width") +
  scale_tintshade_continuous(guide = guide_tintshade(type="crossed")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "yellow", "black"))

Q: npm warns about memory leak in a transitive dependency of bcrypt A:

It appears that bcrypt is not being maintained, despite getting ~ 2M downloads a week on NPM...

https://github.com/kelektiv/node.bcrypt.js/issues/1038

https://github.com/kelektiv/node.bcrypt.js/issues/1189

@mapbox/node-pre-gyp has a newer version out, but this hasn't been adopted by bcrypt (at the time of this writing at least).

I'm considering using this instead: https://github.com/uswriting/bcrypt

Q: Connection to daemon was invalidated A:

Same issue without using Firebase at all. What I did: Delete build folder and compile again. Issue does not appears again.

On Xcode: Clean the Build Folder This will delete all of the products and intermediate files in the build folder. To clean the build folder you can use the shortcut Command+Option+Shift+K or Menu Bar → Product → Hold Option Key → Clean build Folder.

On Flutter: Just delete build folder.

Q: How do I create a custom header in Magento 2 using HTML and CSS A:

Header files for magento is stored in app/design/frontend/package/theme/template/page/html/header.phtml . Now in that you can do your changes. Make sure you take a backup in case something goes wrong. Make sure you clear your cache when u change something in header or footer in order for that to reflect.

Now since you want to use majority of HTML and CSS for your formatting. PHTML files are basically those who use PHP and HTML. You can practically do anything in PHTML files that you will do in HTML so no worries on that part. Just remember whatever you write there will be present in all front end pages so if you write some heavy script for homepage irrespective if you require that elsewhere it will be used everywhere.

If you are new and want to learn magento development try out Magento PHP developers guide by Allan MacGregor. Its one of the best books out there. All the best.

Q: Read and display miliseconds A:

%S is for integer seconds, %OS is for partial seconds. You only need one or the other. No need to set options(). Just use:

library(readr)

parse_time(c("03:44:43.300 PM", "03:44:43.301 PM"), "%I:%M:%OS %p")
#15:44:43.300
#15:44:43.301

I added second time value for illustrative purposes as readr drops trailing zeros by default.
